definition: A parallel shift is when every interest rate on the curve, across all maturities, moves up or down together by roughly the same amount.
core_idea: Parallel shifts tend to be driven by broad forces — credit quality concerns or deliberate government action to add or remove money from the economy — and generally signal a large change in overall economic conditions.
key_points: Contrasts with a change in curve shape (steepening/flattening), where different maturities move by different amounts.
Common triggers cited: shifts in perceived credit quality, or monetary policy actions injecting or withdrawing money from the economy.
relationships: Related to interest rate curve shape as a distinct mode of interest rate movement
